title: Hi-Time: Hierarchical Latent Prediction for Multivariate Time Series Classification
topic: General Machine Learning->Sequential, Network, and Time Series Modeling
claim: A staged pipeline turns raw inputs into hierarchical discrete codes that a model predicts coarse-to-fine before the final decision.
layout: 3 staged dashed panels, left-to-right then bottom row, with loss formulas
description: A three-stage architecture diagram in dashed boxes. Stage 1 (left) takes multivariate time series, downsamples them to multiple scales, and passes them through a backbone and a multi-view representation fusion block. The fusion block has multi-scale, cross-variable and temporal-dynamics fusion, drawn as purple 3D cubes. It outputs a frozen temporal representation. Stage 2 (top right) uses residual quantization. At each of three levels, a vector is compared with its nearest centroid in a codebook, and the centroid is subtracted to give a residual. The levels are color-coded green, blue and orange, and illustrated by a soldier image that sharpens from coarse to fine. Stage 3 (bottom right) has an LLM with MLP heads that predict the three semantic codes in sequence. The codes are concatenated as a condition for classification. Loss formulas L1 and L2 are shown. A legend sits at top right.
caption: The overall architecture of the proposed Hi-Time framework, which comprises three key phases: (1) Temporal Representation
abstract: Integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into time series tasks has yielded impressive performance. While some works aim to enhance accuracy by explicitly designing step-by-step reasoning into prompts, such explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) approaches are difficult to generalize to time series. This is because it is difficult to clearly define the reasoning trajectories of time series. In addition, the high heterogeneity across time series often requires specialized prompt designs, limiting the model's scalability. To address these challenges, we propose Hi-Time , a hi erarchical latent prediction framework based on temporal semantic codes for multivariate time series classification. This framework automatically constructs scenario-specific coarse-to-fine prediction trajectories based on the characteristics of time series, thereby providing structured supervision for the LLM. Specifically, Hi-Time first performs temporal representation pre-training with a multi-view temporal representation fusion to acquire high-quality temporal embeddings. We then discretize these temporal embeddings into hierarchical temporal semantic codes that form the coarse-to-fine prediction trajectory. Finally, the LLM predicts temporal semantic codes in a stepwise manner and then infers the final label, thereby establishing a coarse-to-fine decision process. Experiments on ten public multivariate time series datasets demonstrate that Hi-Time effectively adapts to diverse datasets and outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Our code is available at .
